evidence.citation: Rufinus, Historia ecclesiastica10.9 (=first book of continuation, chapter9), entire Latin chapter
evidence.finding: The newly read complete chapter gives two young relatives of the Tyrian Meropius, with Edesius the younger and Frumentius the other, surviving the ship massacre. Edesius becomes the unnamed king’s cupbearer, Frumentius keeper of records; they assist the widow/child king, then Edesius returns to Tyre. The decisive final sentence identifies Edesius as subsequently a TYRIAN PRESBYTER and Rufinus’s own informant, formerly Frumentius’s companion. This closes the actual primary gap behind the owned Axum king-list scope, beyond the previously read secondary likely-Ousanas identification. It supplies no connection to Ammianus’s ex-master of the rolls or Eunapius’s Cappadocian/Pergamene philosopher.
evidence.qualification: Rufinus names neither the king Ousanas/EllaAmida nor the modern Gregorian year of the capture, regency, ordination or Edesius’s death. The narrative says India ulterior, not the modern country-name Ethiopia at this point; localization is contextual scholarship. His two pupils are propinqui/relatives, not explicitly nephews or biological brothers in this Latin chapter. Constantine’s reign and Athanasius’s recently assumed priesthood are narrative anchors, not exact birthday/death data. No355 death is established. The three owned scopes remain unbridged; different roles alone are not a new proof of biological impossibility.
evidence.accounting: One genuinely new named primary target; already-read owned source passages are retained as old evidence, not counted again.

evidence.citation: Theodoret, Historia religiosa7a–b, complete GREEK chapter, Schulze-edition digital witness; site English not treated as critical authority
evidence.finding: The original Greek now actually read identifies Palladius as contemporary/friend of the preceding Symeon, sharing the ascetic life, shut in a small dwelling by the large village IMMAI. It tells of a merchant murdered during the local fair, his corpse placed at Palladius’s door, a false accusation and a reported miracle exposing the actual murderer. The final portion separately introduces ABRAHAM of Paratomos and his tomb’s healings. These concrete locality/ascetic/companion discriminators supply the missing original hermit biography, distinct as a source scope from the already-read agricultural writer’s OpusAgriculturae preface; the Greek never attributes that agricultural work to this recluse.
evidence.qualification: The miracle is a hagiographic report, not an independently verified forensic event. The merchant’s death is not Palladius’s death, and the tomb/healing conclusion concerns Abraham, not Palladius. No309/390 death, birth year or patriarchal office is given. The webpage openly flags a damaged digital Greek word at the small-dwelling phrase; the name, locality and narrative subject are legible. Its fresh modern English translation was consulted only as an aid, not used to override Greek or claimed as a historic critical edition. No manuscript/printed-image autopsy is claimed; a missing biological equivalence bridge to the agricultural author remains.

Do not claim different full names alone are an absolute biological exclusion; provide a conservative exact-key split with no proven whole-record equivalence. The third delegations/judgments in X1700 do not mean three ordinary consulships.

evidence.citation: Porphyry AdMarcellam, Zimmern1896 published translation, complete letter1–34, personal marriage1–4 especially; JeromeEp127.1–11 newly read in full (12–14 explicitly old reread)
evidence.finding: Porphyry’s own address explicitly says he married Marcella after the death of her previous husband, his friend, despite her five DAUGHTERS and two SONS; he describes their ten months together and his absence on Greek affairs. This is now an actual direct family/marriage witness, beyond the old Eunapius summary. Newly read Jerome127.2 instead describes the Roman Marcella’s husband dying after less than seven months of marriage, her mother ALBINA pressing the aged CEREALIS’s suit and Marcella refusing remarriage in favor of permanent chastity; Jerome repeatedly contrasts seven MONTHS of her marriage with biblical Anna’s seven YEARS. The two explicit marital narratives are incompatible as literal accounts of the same widow’s course, supplying a positive source-account exclusion for the exact two-key split, rather than merely different religion/place.
evidence.qualification: Jerome is a commemorative Christian eulogy and Porphyry a philosophical spousal address, so the exclusion concerns the actual source narratives, not a claim that every rhetorical detail is externally proved. The old extracted Eunapius passage reports five children while the new letter reports five daughters plus two sons; preserve that transmitted discrepancy pending original Greek critical collation. Anna’s84years in Jerome is NOT Marcella’s age. The ten months together is not a death date; no precise Porphyry-wife birthday, marriage year or death follows. Roman325/410 dates must not be transferred to the philosopher’s wife. Published translations were actually read; no claim to Greek/Latin manuscript autopsy.

evidence.finding: The new personal unit explicitly calls Ursinus the rival ordained alongside Damasus and says he was expelled from Rome and appointed bishop at Naples. This reinforces the ecclesiastical source scope of the Ammianus key. The separate owned GLQ888555 is already independently identified as the Alamannic king Ursicinus in Ammianus18.2, not this Roman election rival. Propose exact-key review separation and preserve uncertainty over the late Naples claim.
evidence.qualification: Do not treat the late Naples appointment as independently established, add a precise exile/death year, or infer physical impossibility solely from different roles/places. evidence.finding: New complete Herodian1.8.1–8 explicitly distinguishes Lucilla HUSBAND POMPEIANUS, loyal to Commodus and not told of her plot, from the YOUNG SENATOR QUINTIANUS recruited through Quadratus to stab the emperor. The latter announces that the senate sent him, is seized before striking and DIES after the attempt. New complete Dio73.4 likewise names Claudius Pompeianus as the sword-bearing attacker betrothed to Lucilla daughter, separately calls Lucilla husband Pompeianus, and places the attacker destruction in the plot aftermath. Matching the unique entrance/weapon/senate-announcement event bridges Dio attacker ClaudiusPompeianus to Herodian named Quintianus, rather than treating two name forms as two separate assassins. New Dio74.3.1 then directly identifies the OLDER CLAUDIUS POMPEIANUS as Pertinax former military patron and says the author himself saw him alive participating in the senate UNDER PERTINAX. Thus the already-dead attempted assassin under Commodus and the senior Pompeianus alive under his successor Pertinax are positively different men. This gives both an explicit role/relationship discriminator and an incompatible death-versus-survival chronology for the exact two owned QID scopes.
evidence.qualification: Do not invent a precise paternal relationship from these chapters: Herodian calls the attacker Quintianus and Lucilla husband Pompeianus but does not call the attacker that husbands biological son; Dio describes betrothal to Lucilla daughter, not nephewship of the husband. Dio73.4 is complete, Dio74.3.1 entire named old-Pompeianus personal unit and adjacent honor context are complete, Herodian1.8 all eight sections complete; other unrelated portions of both Dio books are not claimed as newly checked people. evidence.citation: CILVI708,1027,1603,2129,2130 BOTH units,2269,2270: seven complete records; current EDCS editions
evidence.finding: New complete VI1603 names the dedicator Ti(berius)IuliusBalbillus, sacerdosSolis, honoring annona-prefect ClaudiusJulianus, under the Fabianus/Mucianus consular pair andXIIIKalFeb. New complete VI2129 again names Ti(berius)IuliusBalbillus, sacerdosSolis, honoring chiefVestal NumisiaMaximilla under the SAME consular pair on IdJan. New complete VI2269 explicitly honors Ti(berio)IulioBalbillo, sacerdosSolisElagabali, by his freedman EUDAEMON. These are exactly the THREE distinctive events the owned Q15982239 modern TITUS article attributes to Titus (Jan15/Jan20,201 and Eudemon patron). Their currently published primary transcriptions instead explicitly read TI/TIBERIUS. New VI2270 additionally honors TiIulBalbillus on KalJan under AnullinusII/Fronto;VI1027 has the same199 consular pair and bare IuliusBalbillus dedicating to Severus. Thus the two modern QID scopes concretely overlap a named TIBERIUS priest-core; the prior Titus-vs-Tiberius split cannot be retained as if independently proved by these objects. New complete VI2130 instead names AURELIUSIULIUSBALBILLUS honoring TerentiaFlavola and dates its second face under LaetusII/Cerialis (catalogue215). That extra name/role correspondence is compatible with, but does not expressly prove, the modern article claim that the Tiberius priest added Aurelius after212. The remaining whole-source issue is now specifically this215 Aurelius link plus the modern two-article construction, rather than an assumed separate Titus201 attestation.
evidence.qualification: Critical boundary: the readings/expansions TI/TIBERIUS are those of the actual complete EDCS original-text publication; no stone photograph or independent printed-CIL scan was inspected. The cited Halsberghe53–55/78 and Wacher697 books have not independently been read here, so the exact origin of the modern TITUS heading and the two-priest/kinship assertion remains a bibliographic gap. This candidate does not prove that no other TitusBalbillus ever existed; it says these specifically cited201/benefactor objects do not independently attest TITUS. The215 text literally has AureliusIulius, not TiIulius; adding Aurelius because of the212 citizenship grant is an interpretation, not stated on this object, and does not itself prove the same man or a father-son/adoption link. Shared uncommon name, Roman cult and city support overlap but are not silently promoted to an unconditional whole-row duplicate redirect. VI708 merely says IuliusBalbillus and does not repair the215 praenomen question. No inscription read establishes descent from AntiochusI, kinship to JuliaDomna or that the two modern article subjects are relatives. EDCS199/201/215 are catalogue conversions of the printed consular/day formulas: no new independent Fasti/calendar collation was performed. KalJan,IdJan,XIIIKalFeb andpridNonApr are dates of honors/dedications, not personal birthdays or deaths, and their earliest surviving attestation is not a first appointment. Final-after-this-no-more-known is not death. All old evidence/limits and unknown endpoints remain; no game change or full duplicate_of is proposed.

evidence.citation: Sanguozhi30: entire Yiyimo succession/Wigung birth-and-royal-events unit, Seisaku lines30–32; Sanguozhi28: complete Guanqiu-Jian Goguryeo royal-campaign unit including Deulae and Wang Qi; Korean official SamgukSagi17 accession unit rechecked
evidence.finding: New Sanguozhi30 directly makes WIGUNG the son and successor of YIYIMO, then identifies this same named king by three concrete royal events: helping Sima Yi against Gongsun Yuan in Jingchu2, attacking Xianping in Zhengshi3, and defeat by Guanqiu Jian in Zhengshi5. New Sanguozhi28 independently narrates the actual Goguryeo royal opponent GONG in the complete Guanqiu-Jian campaign unit: twenty-thousand troops at Feiliushui/Liangkou, destruction of Wandu, the remonstrant DEULAE, the royal family flight, and Wang Qi chasing him through Okjeo in the following Zhengshi6 campaign. These are the same distinctive king, opponent, campaign geography and named subordinate episode as the already-read SamgukSagi17 DONGCHEON/UWIGEO narrative, which explicitly places the Deulae/Guanqiu-Jian episode under Dongcheon. The currently rechecked official Korean accession original independently spells Dongcheon, alternate title Dongyang, personal name Uwigeo, childhood name Gyoche and son of Sansang. Thus the Chinese Wigung/Gong WAR KING is bridged to the Korean Dongcheon/Uwigeo WAR KING by a specific multi-event narrative identity, not merely by similar names or a modern normalized alias. The different older SamgukSagi16 attribution of Wigung/eyes-open birth etymology to Sansang is adjudicated as an explicit disagreement in the transmitted genealogy/name allocation; it is preserved, not silently made consistent or assigned a second universal lifespan.
evidence.qualification: This closes the identity of the named royal actor across the specific owned biography and the original war accounts, while NOT deciding that every transmitted royal name genealogy is historically correct. The Chinese original does NOT literally write the Korean name Uwigeo or the title Dongcheon; their correspondence is an explicitly explained inference from the unusually specific matching events. SamgukSagi17 itself criticizes Tongjian attributing Deulae advice to Wigung; retain that contrary ancient editorial judgment as a real disagreement, not proof the Chinese original lacks Wigung. Sanguozhi30 dates the first defeat Zhengshi5(244) and28 the renewed expedition Zhengshi6(245), whereas SamgukSagi17 collects the war in royal year20(246 under its own accession scheme). This chronological discrepancy remains unresolved and does not defeat the identification of the same uniquely described royal opponent. Chinese Yiyimo genealogy also need not validate all Korean preceding-generation identifications. The earlier209/248 birth/death statements and lunar ninth months remain source-reported chronologies; this candidate introduces no exact biological endpoints or Gregorian month conversions. All old primary evidence, reported genealogical contradiction and limitations are retained. Native Wikisource downloads timed out: the successful actual web-tool primary personal-unit readings are cached, not falsely described as native full-volume downloads or manuscript autopsy. evidence.citation: Sozomen HE6.29; original QID verified Paul I biography
evidence.excerpt: Παῦλος μὲν ἐν Φέρμῃ
evidence.finding: 对应完整本人段已读，两个keys显不同身份；原Wiki所用部分已读但未把长文缓存9000字称全文。

Palladius Lausiac20 was read in its entirety: Paul is a Pherme/Scete ascetic whose distinguishing practice is300 prayers counted by pebbles, and who consults Macarius. This positively matches Sozomen6.29’s same personal practice, not the Constantinopolitan episcopal succession. Socrates2.26 explicitly narrates the bishop Paul’s strangling at Cucusus. No calendar life dates are inferred for the monk; Macarius’s sixty years and the virgin’s thirty years belong to them, not Paul. Distinct contextual identities support separation; no unprovided precise monk-survival year is invented.

Ammianus31.13–14 narrates the emperor Valens’ death at Adrianople and explicitly says he was almost fifty. Socrates1.27/31 already places Valens of Mursa among the adult bishop-investigators under Constantine at the Tyre affair. Under the well-established378/335 event chronology the future emperor would be about seven, not the existing bishop. This is a positive age-and-office exclusion, not just different titles; retain the approximate age and do not convert it into a new exact328 birth. The two alternatives for the emperor’s fatal injury/burning are variant accounts of one emperor, not two extra identities.

evidence.citation: Rufinus Historia ecclesiastica10.9, full Latin Frumentius/Edesius chapter
evidence.finding: The full newly read chapter directly follows Frumentius from Meropius’s young relative to the unnamed king’s records official, assistant to the regent/child king and promoter of Roman merchants’ Christian meetings, then his report to Athanasius and episcopal commission back to India. Rufinus expressly identifies former companion Edesius, later a presbyter in Tyre, as his personal informant. This adds a concrete early literary witness and its claimed chain of testimony to the already-closed Frumentius source core.
evidence.qualification: This is an already-closed identity receiving a new original source, not a new whole-identity closure. The king is unnamed, Athanasius is only recently installed, and the chapter gives no exact birth/death or modern conversion year. Ousanas/Ezana identification and literal modern Ethiopia-vs-India geography are not silently read into the Latin. Rufinus’s reported apostolic miracles are source testimony, not independently proved events; the return/commission is an activity sequence, not a first-career date.
evidence.accounting: One genuinely new named primary target; already-read owned source passages are retained as old evidence, not counted again.

evidence.citation: Thorigny CIL XIII3162, all THREE complete inscribed units including both copied letters; RIB1280 full edition/diplomatic text, apparatus and internal-date context
evidence.finding: Thorigny’s main face directly names TIBERIUS CLAUDIUS PAULINUS as legate of LUGDUNENSIS, then explicitly says the SAME man later served as legate in BRITAIN with the sixth legion, with Sollemnis attending him. The copied Paulinus letter itself addresses Sennius Sollemnis and discusses gifts, a future military commission and pay; the Aedinius letter explicitly makes Paulinus his predecessor. This is a concrete original inter-office identity bridge. RIB1280 independently preserves TibClPau[...], the restored legate name/rank and a building carried out SUB CURA in the emperor Antoninus’s TRP III/COS III setting, internally dated to220 under Elagabalus. This supplies a real active early-third-century governing context, unlike a retrospective honor’s bare catalogue date. The separate owned law addresses a serving EpirusNova governor under Valentinian/Valens in372: keeping the two named provincial-source scopes as one ordinary adult career would require another152years after Paulinus’s220 command. Propose their clear chronological source separation.
evidence.qualification: The exact RIB reading is partly restored and its imperial name/numerals are erased; preserve the published apparatus and internal220 dating rather than claiming unbroken stone text. The Thorigny base’s Pius/Proculus subscription dates its238 installation; the copied letters are earlier and it does not prove Paulinus or Aedinius survived238, died238, or personally wrote then. A letter’s promised future commission is not an already held post for Sollemnis; the twenty-five-thousand sestertii is his pay, not Paulinus’s age. The220 SUB CURA commission and372 governor address are the positive chronological discriminator, not merely a152year gap between potentially posthumous monuments. Unknown biological endpoints remain null and game228 death is not applied to the Epirus person.
evidence.accounting: One new named target record; number of monuments, diploma copies or differently named people inside the composite is not inflated into extra completed roster people.

evidence.citation: CIL II4121/II14.984 complete cursus; II4122/II14.985 both complete units including subordinate names; III7516 entire surviving fragment; ILB642 entire surviving altar; VI1978 complete surviving priestly admissions; Ashmolean HCR135387 complete object record and BOTH actual specimen photographs
evidence.finding: The full Tarraco honor explicitly names QUINTUS HEDIUS, son of LUCIUS, POLLIA tribe, RUFUS LOLLIANUS GENTIANUS: augur, consul, proconsul of Asia, census/legation roles in Lugdunensis and Hispania citerior, curator of Puteoli and Velitrae, commander of XXII Primigenia and tribune of VII Gemina. The second honor explicitly names Quintus Hedius Lollianus Gentianus as Hispania citerior governor, with his own corn clerks, commentarienses and speculatores listed separately. This independently establishes the full Hedius core beyond the modern biography. The separate Moesian fragment III7516 prints Cosco/[nium Gentianum] in its Commodus imperial/legate context; ILB642 prints abbreviated COS GEN beside a partially restored Cn Suellius Rufus. Most decisively for the abbreviated Cosconius core, the newly viewed actual Ashmolean coin photograph has the legible reverse COSC GENTIANOU within the Nicopolis-ad-Istrum legend, opposite Septimius Severus. These are concrete different full-name/province source cores. No original object read here states that Cosconius is an alternative nomen of Hedius or joins the two careers.
evidence.qualification: The coin object catalogue assigns196 according to RPC; there is no engraved CE year, so196 is an editorial dating, not an exact life endpoint. CILIII7516 is heavily restored, including much of the provincial title and imperial titulature; its190–193 catalogue interval is not a birth/death date. ILB642 has damaged abbreviations and a catalogue198 date: it must not by itself create a certain simultaneous two-governor career. The Hedius honors have null numeric dates. VI1978 partly RESTORES the Hedius cognomina in a dated priest-admission series; admission is not birth and the surrounding other priests are not relatives. The separately read157–159 Lucius Hedius Rufus Lollianus AVITUS texts are not assigned to Quintus Gentianus. Different nomina and distinct provincial careers support conservative key separation, not biological proof that a polyonymous official could never bear both names; whole identity remains unclosed.
evidence.accounting: One newly read roster target per row; multiple original objects and internal source identities do not inflate the person count; exact-key partition refinement is not whole-person closure.

This independently reads the previously unexamined Moesian governor coin core behind the old PIR entry, whereas the already-read separate honor names MARCUS ULPIUS TERTULLIANUS AQUILA without a Moesian office. evidence.qualification: Only the actual reverse photograph was personally inspected; the obverse was read through the complete scholarly printed legend, not an unseen image. RPC241–244 is the issue-date assignment under Gordian/Tranquillina, not the governor birth/death or first appointment. HYPATEIA is a provincial magistrate formula, not proof that he held an ordinary Roman consulship. Do not import the catalogue expanded Prosius into the engraved legend or treat that modern expansion alone as proof against Marcus Ulpius. The old undated Aquila honor remains valid and preserved; the separate Attalea curator stone has not newly been obtained. One owned PIR key contains both historical hypotheses, so it stays ONE partition with both accounts and no duplicate key.

evidence.citation: Symmachus Ep3.23–29, all seven complete original Latin letters in PL witness; Zosimus5.45 complete Marinianus/Maximilianus event context, published1814 translation
evidence.finding: The actual seven letters now read identify Marinianus as the legal teacher/forensic expert whom Symmachus invites to rest, congratulate a marriage/new child, discuss winter clothing and intended return home, and exchange greetings. Newly read Zosimus5.45 explicitly makes a Marinianus the FATHER ransoming captured Maximilianus for thirty-thousand gold pieces, within the Alaric/Rome crisis and the Heliocrates/Attalus narrative. That sentence supplies no legal title, Galatian origin, former Spanish vicariate or connection to the378 Syrian craftsman. The complete original units remove the previously genuine reading gap while leaving those modern career/family equivalences as hypotheses.
evidence.qualification: The displayed PL digital witness has apparent Tebet/forenses tabulas in3.23 where the locator literature gives Tenet/forenses rabulas;3.24 has both filium and filiolae forms;3.25 prints Gallatia. Do not silently replace these with a modern critical text, decide Galatia versus Spanish Gallaecia, or identify the newborn as Zosimus’s Maximilianus. Neither the letters nor the quoted Zosimus personal event states a CE year.383 belongs only to the previously read law’s addressed vicarius, and378 only to the previously read craftsman monument. A modern409 dating of the ransom remains contextual, not an exact historical death or an automatic repair of game death406 across the composite. The Zosimus witness is a published English translation, not newly read Greek.
evidence.accounting: One new named primary target record; already-read passages/metadata are explicitly not recounted.

evidence.citation: Gawlikowski, Les princes de Palmyre, Syria62(1985)251–261, complete eleven pages; inscriptions2,13 and fragment12 especially
evidence.finding: Tomb inscription2 gives Septimius Odaenathus son of Hairan, grandson of Wahballath, descendant of Nasor; newly published13, NisanSE563/April252, repeats that complete genealogy with clarissimus/exarch role. The owned old PIR S338 tomb genealogy is thus directly bridged to the exarch whose public career continues in the king’s honors; the elder ancestor was an old prosopographical reconstruction, not a separately dated tomb owner. Adopt the author’s one-person re-identification for the two owned keys, while preserving dissent and the contrary literary tradition below. This is adjudication of the source referents, not proof that every ancient/modern account agrees.
evidence.qualification: Anonymous post-Dio fragment12 literally distinguishes an elder Odaenathus killed by Rufinus and a younger Odaenathus complaining of his father’s murder. Gawlikowski’s identification of the complainant as Vaballathus is an editorial conjecture, not the Greek wording. Old modern-source notice of Balty’s dissent remains; Balty2002 original was not read in this batch. Tomb2 is undated and built for himself/descendants, not a death record. Nisan563 is the monument’s date. Circa220 birth and267/268 death in the discussion are reconstructions and are not imported as exact historical BD. Greek restorations in13 remain visible; original images253/254/256/257 were inspected because OCR is imperfect.

evidence.finding: Durostorum尤利乌斯27年军役/7campaign/Maximus审判是旧军士，原页304标约且列292/302传统，255无独立出生原证；节日May27不作死亡日。德国Caerleon原页未读，但比较ENJuliusAaron是Britain城legions殉道、Gildas/Bede后世记录，与多瑙河Durostorum不同地点传统，隔离；未实读Gildas或VeteranActs不声明primaryclosed。

evidence.citation: Gildas De excidio, Migne/CorpusCorporum chapterVII–VIII complete persecution/martyr units; Passio Iuli Veterani1–4 complete Latin, Musurillo1972 pp260,262,264; correct German Julius von Caerleon full short biography oldid271711730
evidence.finding: The correct German owned page is now read and identifies the British Julius alongside Aaron, citing Gildas. The new Gildas original calls Aaron and Julius citizens of Legionum urbs, within the British martyr narrative, then distinguishes Alban’s escape/miracles from the others’ torture. The complete new Latin Veteran Act instead presents Julius before Maximus,27years of service and seven campaigns, military veteran status, refusal of the bonus, trial and beheading; fellow prisoner Isichius and previously dead Valentio are distinct named subjects. These source scopes should be separated for review, not collapsed under one modern Julius date.
evidence.qualification: Gildas does not explicitly write Caerleon, only Legionum urbs; its modern precise localization and German303/304 chronology are interpretations. The Latin Veteran Act itself supplies neither Durostorum nor an absolute consular death year: Musurillo’s note conditionally obtains the place from the Roman Martyrology and proposes early304. Its27years is service duration, not age at death; the ten-year bonus is not another ten personal years. May27/June22 feasts are not exact execution dates. Musurillo’s Latin veteran wording does not unambiguously establish re-enlistment despite the English rendering. No255 birth or unique292/302/304 death is established.
evidence.accounting: One new named primary subject; shared pages are not additional people. Older diplomas/catalogue/secondary readings are not recounted.

evidence.citation: CIL XVI139 complete surviving diploma units; RMD IV307 and IV317/V457 complete diploma units; CIL VI31318a entire fragment; RPC VI1363 complete printed obverse/reverse legends and object entry
evidence.finding: New XVI139 explicitly dates the diploma VIIIdusIanuarias under CAIUS VETTIUS GRATUS and MARCUS VITELLIUS SELEUCUS, under ElagabalusTRPIV/COSIII. New RMDIV307 independently gives the same pair IIIKalendasDecembres, with full imperial titulature and the veteran/family grant; thus the221 consular core is now checked in original documents, not only PIR/modern biography. VI31318a directly prints Marcus Flavius Vitellius Seleucus in a Commodus-dated setting, with no official title in the surviving short text. Newly read RPCVI1363 actually publishes the reverse Greek abbreviation IULANTSELEUKOU under the Marcianopolitan provincial formula, opposite Elagabalus and JuliaMaesa, confirming the separately named IuliusAntoniusSeleucus coin-governor core. None of these objects names the bare Seleucus of the usurper list as a rebel or states a usurper/consul/governor identity bridge.
evidence.qualification: The221 subscriptions date grants and use consular eponyms; they are not Seleucus’s autograph, birth/death or proof he personally survived to theNovember grant. The twenty-eight years of service and named wife/children in RMDIV307 belong to veteran GaiusJuliusMontanus, not to the consul; the7 witnesses are not his relatives. RMDIV317 has extensive restoration and should not be treated as an independent fully preserved name. VI31318a catalogue185–192 and its matching full name do not alone prove an uninterrupted career through221 or a father/son relationship. RPC’s expanded Iulius/Antonius and provincial legatus title must be distinguished from abbreviated preserved legend and from an ordinary Roman consulship; the coin gives no exact year. The actual coin images were NOT inspected: the two BritishMuseum image endpoints timed out. Only the complete published legend/object record was read; keep that visual gap explicit. No220 usurper death or whole-record date patch is established.
evidence.accounting: One new named target record; number of monuments, diploma copies or differently named people inside the composite is not inflated into extra completed roster people.

evidence.citation: CIL VIII9365=20994+21056 / ILS1099, complete currently joined text; CIL III7505 / ILS2311 entire veteran dedication
evidence.finding: The joined original honor explicitly gives SEXTUS CORNELIUS, son of Sextus, Palatina tribe, CLEMENS, consul and DUX OF THE THREE DACIAS. Its dedicator is Avidius Valens, former consular beneficiarius, with restored centurion/legion wording. Independently III7505 makes veteran Titus Valerius Marcianus discharged IN DACIA UNDER CORNELIUS CLEMENS, under the Cethegus/Clarus consular pair, after eastern/German campaigns under the listed commanders. Together they provide the previously missing full-nomen plus exact-province/military-context bridge for Dio’s Dacian Clemens, beyond merely repeating a modern normalized source-key name. Propose the ordinary historical identification of that Dacian command core as Sextus Cornelius Clemens; no connection is thereby made to the other four differently named owned Clemens scopes.
evidence.qualification: Dio itself still says only Clemens. The identification rests on the matching Dacian command context and explicit Cornelius in the veteran document plus full Sextus Cornelius in the honor, not a claim that the literary text spells the praenomen. VIII20994+21056 is a scholarly joining of fragments, not two independent full honors; its numerical date is null. III7505 catalogue171–200 dates the veteran’s monument, not the discharge or Clemens’s lifespan. The AntoninusIV enlistment, military campaigns, retirement and family Marcia Basilissa/Valeria Longa concern the VETERAN, not Clemens. No absolute death, birth or first appointment is supplied; the inscribed Cethegus/Clarus names are retained without converting this into a precise personal life year. Older source-scope separations and uncertain dates remain.
evidence.accounting: One new named target record; number of monuments, diploma copies or differently named people inside the composite is not inflated into extra completed roster people.
